correctness.rationale: For every bounded positive operator and rank-one positive input, factor the crossed expression into two rank-one terms and the ordinary expression into one rank-one term. Hilbert–Schmidt expansion and the Gram/exterior-square identity yield exact trace and Frobenius defects. Positivity follows from covariance and Cauchy–Schwarz; strictness follows from spectral support and non-affinity of distinct power functions. Two positive singular values give strict Schatten-p monotonicity and the unique crossing. Exact rational witness: \(\|H_t\|_2^2=1004/3\), \(\|C_t\|_2^2=952/3\), \((s_1s_2)^2=724/9\), and the squared trace-norm defect is \(4(\sqrt{181}-13)/3>0\). A finite checker confirms the algebra but cannot certify infinite-dimensional claims.

value.rationale: The spectral-support formula classifies the trace and Hilbert–Schmidt directions for the complete natural rank-one input family, in arbitrary Hilbert dimension, and gives an exact unique Schatten-p transition. Its smallest-dimensional trace-norm witness is analytically certified at the classical central-interval endpoint, making a substantive refinement of the known dimension-three obstruction rather than an arbitrary or routine numerical example.
